observed_result:
The recent-participation record, the learning gate and the fast-change bounds are implemented in package plasticity and wired into learning.Individual through EnablePlasticity, DisablePlasticity and AdvanceGated. 18 tests pass in the three filters above.

A. Package level, three-neuron chain (edges 0 = 0->1, 1 = 1->2, 2 = 0->2 disabled), rule decay_e = decay_p = 0.5, plastic_max = 8, w_min = 0.0625. Every decay is a power of two, so the tables are exact in float64 and the tests compare with ==.

A1 closed gate (TestGateZeroLetsPlasticOnlyDecay). Activity y = [1,1,1] at every step, the fast state seeded at plastic = 2, gate = 0:
  eligibility 1, 1.5, 1.75 (it keeps tracking activity)
  plastic     1, 0.5, 0.25 (it only decays; nothing is added)

A2 delayed gate (TestDelayedGateUsesResidualEligibility). Activity only at step 0, gate 0, 0, 1:
  decay_e 0.5:  eligibility 1, 0.5, 0.25   -> plastic 0, 0, 0.25
  decay_e 0.25: eligibility 1, 0.25, 0.0625 -> plastic 0, 0, 0.0625
  The fast change is exactly the residual eligibility, and the two decays give distinguishable results (0.25 versus 0.0625).

A3 decay (TestEligibilityAndPlasticDecayToZero). From eligibility = plastic = 4 with no activity and no gate, both fall strictly at every one of 60 steps and end below 1e-12 (4 * 2^-60 is about 3.5e-18).

A4 bound (TestPlasticMaxClampsAndCounts). decay_e = decay_p = 0.5, unit activity, open gate, plastic_max 1.5. The unbounded series 1, 2, 2.5 is reported as plastic 1, 1.5, 1.5 with clamped 0, 1, 1. The mirror with post = -1 gives -1, -1.5, -1.5 with the same counts.

A5 sign safety (TestEffectiveHoldsFixedSignEdgesAtWMin). base [0.5, -0.25, 0.75], signs [+1, -1, 0], plastic [-2, -2] on edges 0 and 1:
  fixed signs -> [0.0625, -0.0625, 0.75], held_at_w_min 2, and w[k] * sign > 0 for both fixed edges
  every edge free -> [-1.5, -2.25, 0.75], held_at_w_min 0 (a free edge is allowed to cross zero)
  Edge 2 has no plasticity and keeps its base value in both cases.

A6 refusals: Effective refuses 5 malformed conversions (short base, wrong sign length, a sign outside -1/0/+1, a non-finite base weight, a state built for another model).

B. Individual level, two-neuron LIF fixture: nodes 0 and 1, one instantaneous edge 0->1, dt = tau = tau_syn = 1 so lambda = kappa = exp(-1) = 0.36787944117144233 and alpha = 1 - exp(-1) = 0.6321205588285577; theta_min 0.05, theta_max 1, theta_raw -2 so theta = 0.16324277592101166; v_reset -0.5, no refractory step; base weight 0.9; encoder and readout are the identity onto neuron 0 and off neuron 1, so the only rounding left is Insyra's float32 readout boundary. Input [1.5, 0, 1.5, 0, 0]. Rule as above; the pre signal is the synaptic trace after the step and the post signal is that step's 0/1 event. The expected columns were computed from these closed forms by an independent Python implementation of the LIF step and of the rule, before the Go integration existed, and matched it to the last bit.

B1 open gate at every step (TestGatedAdvanceFollowsTheHandComputedOrder):
  step | weight the core integrated | trace0 | event1 | eligibility | plastic | readout
  0 | 0.9                | 1                   | 0 | 0                   | 0                   | 0
  1 | 0.9                | 0.36787944117144233 | 1 | 0.36787944117144233 | 0.36787944117144233 | 1
  2 | 1.2678794411714422 | 1.1353352832366128  | 0 | 0.18393972058572117 | 0.36787944117144233 | 0.3678794503211975
  3 | 1.2678794411714422 | 0.41766650953930634 | 1 | 0.5096363698321669  | 0.693576090417888   | 1.1353353261947632
  4 | 1.593576090417888  | 0.1536509221253469  | 1 | 0.40846910704143036 | 0.7552571522503744  | 1.4176665544509888
  PlasticReport: steps 5, clamped 0, held_at_w_min 0. The step-4 event exists only because the fast change had already raised the weight; at the base weight the same step stays below threshold (see B2).

B2 plain Advance with plasticity enabled is the same call with a gate of zero on every row (TestPlainAdvanceKeepsTheGateClosed): eligibility 0, 0.36787944117144233, 0.18393972058572117, 0.5096363698321669, 0.25481818491608343; plastic 0 throughout; readout 0, 1, 0.3678794503211975, 1.1353353261947632, 0.417666494846344, which is bit for bit the readout of an individual that never enabled the mechanism.

B3 one late gate pulse, gate [0, 0, 0, 1, 0] (TestDelayedGatePulseChangesLaterRows): rows 0 to 3 are bit-identical to B2; the fast change at the moment the gate fires is exactly the residual eligibility 0.5096363698321669, and the weight it produces flips the step-4 event, so the last readout is 1.4176665544509888 instead of 0.417666494846344. The fast change then halves to 0.25481818491608343 because the gate closed again.

B4 fixed sign on a running individual (TestFixedSignEdgeStaysOnItsSignAndCountsTheHold). The edge is declared +1 and stores rho = log(0.9); the fast state is restored at -8 and w_min is 0.9. Without the floor the edge would integrate 0.9 - 8 = -7.1 and become inhibitory. With it the magnitude is held at 0.9 on all five rows (held_at_w_min 5, clamped 0) and the readout is exactly the B2 table; the fast change halves -8, -4, -2, -1, -0.5 and ends at -0.25. The same -8 on a free edge produces an all-zero readout, because the edge really does cross zero there. A fixed-sign edge therefore never crosses zero and the holds are counted per edge and per row.

B5 off restores the reference behaviour (TestAdvanceWithoutPlasticityIsUnchanged), on both the three-neuron LIF fixture and the two-neuron continuous fixture of learning/individual_test.go: a never-enabled individual, an individual that enabled and then disabled the mechanism, and AdvanceGated with an all-zero gate all return the same bits, the disabled individual writes no plastic part, and its PlasticReport is the zero value.

B6 lifecycle (TestEnablePlasticityValidatesAndReplaces): an edge index outside the core is refused; a second EnablePlasticity call replaces the declaration (edges [0,1,2] -> [1]) and restarts the fast state at zero; the pair rule is accepted on the spiking core and refused on the continuous one, because that core emits no events. TestSTDPPairRunsOnTheSpikingIndividual shows the pair rule reaching a real core's events: both per-edge traces persist and the fast change on the 0->1 edge of the B fixture is positive, which is the pre-before-post direction.

B7 gate hygiene (TestAdvanceGatedRejectsMismatchedGates): a gate shorter than the input, a non-finite gate value, and an open gate on an individual whose plasticity is disabled are all errors rather than silent no-ops.

C. Persistence. IndividualSnapshot.Plastic is a *PlasticPart carrying the plasticity.Config and plasticity.State, absent while the mechanism was never enabled. Snapshot and RestoreIndividual round-trip it bit-identically and share no buffer with the caller, and continuing from a restored copy equals continuing from the original (TestPlasticSnapshotRoundTrip). RestoreIndividual refuses 8 malformed parts (unknown rule, edge out of range, no edges, a short state, an over-long state, pair traces under a rate rule, a fast change past the declared bound, a non-finite eligibility). In checkpoint the schema stays coimnet-individual-checkpoint/v1: a saved document carries "plastic":{"config":{"rule":{"kind":"hebbian_rate"..., writes no pre_trace for a rate rule, and an individual that never enabled the mechanism writes no plastic key at all (TestSaveLoadIndividualCarriesThePlasticPart). LoadIndividual refuses 19 malformed plastic blocks (null part, missing config, missing state, missing edges, missing decay_e, missing decay_p, missing w_min, missing kind, unknown kind, null decay_e, missing eligibility, null eligibility, a null inside plastic, a state whose length is not the edge count, a pair trace under a rate rule, an edge out of range, a descending edge list, an empty edge list, an unknown rule field). The same document is still refused by LoadModelPackage, so the three artefacts keep refusing each other. Every pre-existing test in checkpoint/individual_test.go is unchanged.
assumption_statement: This is a hand-computed unit verification on synthetic two- and three-neuron fixtures, not biology and not a task result. The LIF constants were chosen so that lambda, alpha and kappa have closed forms and so that step 4 of the B fixture sits between the drive of the base weight and the drive of the raised weight; that is an engineering choice made to expose the mechanism, not a parameter set derived from any release. The gate is supplied by the caller in this stage, exactly as ticket 18 root decision 4 says: no receptor, no chemical state and no modulation source produces it here, and gate 0 on plain Advance is the root decision for this stage rather than a claim about how a gate arrives in a real protocol. The order inside a step (core forward, then eligibility and pair traces, then the gate, then the next forward with the new effective weights) and the two ordering conventions inside the pair rule are declared modelling choices pinned by test. Fast changes never reach Parameters, and no gradient step was run alongside them here. Nothing in this record exercises a real connectome, a whole-brain run, a runner protocol or a learned task; the runner and comparison work is the second stage of ticket 18 (NAT-06).

limitations: Unit scale only: two- and three-neuron fixtures, at most three edges. No real graph, no whole-brain run, no protocol and no learned task result.
The gate is caller-supplied. MOD-05's receptor-derived gate and time window are not implemented here; only the gate and time-window behaviour of a caller-supplied sequence is shown.
The runner and the three-cell comparison (before, after, off) of ticket 18 stage two are not done, so NAT-06 has no evidence yet.

stdp_pair on a running individual is verified qualitatively (both traces persist, the fast change has the expected sign) rather than with a hand-computed table against the core's own events; the hand-computed pair tables are at the package level in evidence/LRN-04/.

The B tables were produced by an independent Python implementation of the documented LIF and rule equations, not by a published reference implementation, and are compared to 1e-12 for the derived quantities and exactly for the readout.

The red state for the plasticity package and for the learning integration is a build failure rather than a numeric mismatch, because both the package and the public methods were new. Only the checkpoint red state is behavioural.

A plastic part written as JSON null is refused by the individual checkpoint's existing null scanner before the optional-part walk sees it, so "null means disabled" is only reachable through the in-process snapshot type, not through a saved document. The walk treats null as disabled for consistency with the neural union; the document-level rule is stricter.
One machine, one toolchain: macOS arm64 with go1.26.5. No cross-platform run.
The verification commands ran while other agents held uncommitted work in the same tree, so the full-suite log covers their packages as well as this one.
